a01.title: An LLM gateway for your company
a01.prompt: Every team calls LLM APIs directly with their own keys. Design one gateway: 40 services, 2 million requests a day, peak 5x average, average 1,500 input and 300 output tokens. Needs: per-team budgets, model routing (small vs large), prompt caching, retries, logging of cost per request, and no keys in services.
a01.deliverable: A one-page design: diagram (clients → gateway → providers), the request path, how routing and budgets work, a cost estimate per day at two model prices, and two trade-offs.

a02.title: An evaluation platform for LLM features
a02.prompt: Ten product teams ship prompts and agents. Design a platform that stores eval sets, runs them on every prompt or model change in CI, supports code graders and calibrated model judges, and blocks releases that regress. 50 suites × 200 cases, run on every pull request.
a02.deliverable: Diagram, data model (suite, case, run, score), the CI flow, how judges are calibrated, cost per full run, and what you would cut for version 1.

a03.title: A platform for autonomous data agents
a03.prompt: Agents will triage pipeline failures, answer data questions and propose dbt fixes for 300 data users. Design the runtime: MCP tool servers, permissions, approval gates, budgets, traces and evaluation. Agents must never write to production without approval.
a03.deliverable: Diagram, permission model per tool, the approval flow, what is logged and for how long, how you measure success, and the riskiest failure mode with its mitigation.

s00.title: Your study system as a data product
s00.prompt: Warm-up: design how this app could store your progress for 3 devices with offline use and sync once a day.
s00.deliverable: Five boxes, where state lives, and one conflict case with how you resolve it.

s01.title: Rides analytics from scratch
s01.prompt: A ride-hailing company has 2 million trips a day in 6 cities. Product wants hourly completed trips per city with at most 1 hour delay. Design ingestion, storage, processing, serving and orchestration.
s01.deliverable: Back-of-envelope (events/s, GB/day), a five-box diagram, where each tool sits, and a decision record for Kafka vs direct writes.

s02.title: A lake that survives growth
s02.prompt: Trips grow 10x to 20 million a day. Queries over 2 years of data take minutes and small files keep appearing. Design the table layout and maintenance.
s02.deliverable: Partitioning and sort choices with reasons, file size targets, compaction and snapshot expiry schedule, and before/after query cost estimate.

s03.title: Spark at 20x scale
s03.prompt: The daily Silver job grows from 30 GB to 600 GB and one city is 40% of the data. Design cluster sizing and the job so it finishes within 1 hour.
s03.deliverable: Executor sizing maths, how you handle skew, shuffle partitions, and what you monitor in the Spark UI.

s04.title: A warehouse people trust
s04.prompt: Finance and product disagree on "revenue". Design the dimensional model and the semantic layer so both get the same number.
s04.deliverable: Fact and dimension tables with grain, SCD choices, metric definitions, tests, and ownership.

s05.title: Surge pricing in real time
s05.prompt: Compute supply and demand per city zone every 30 seconds from 50,000 events per second, with late events up to 2 minutes.
s05.deliverable: Streaming topology, windowing and watermarks, state size estimate, exactly-once sink, and what happens when the job restarts.

s06.title: Source of truth with CDC
s06.prompt: Orders live in Postgres (5,000 writes/s). Analytics needs every change in the lakehouse within 5 minutes, including deletes.
s06.deliverable: CDC pipeline, ordering and deduplication, how deletes and schema changes flow, and the reconciliation check.

s07.title: Move it to AWS for under $3,000 a month
s07.prompt: Lift the platform to AWS. Budget $3,000/month. Design services, IAM, networking and cost controls.
s07.deliverable: Service map, IAM roles per job, a monthly cost table, and three cost guardrails.

s08.title: Two engines, one set of tables
s08.prompt: Data science uses Databricks, analytics uses Snowflake. Design storage and governance so both read the same tables without copies.
s08.deliverable: Table format and catalog choice, access control model, lineage, and the interop trade-offs.

s09.title: Reliability you can measure
s09.prompt: The CEO dashboard was wrong three times last quarter. Design SLOs, data contracts, tests and on-call for the top 20 tables.
s09.deliverable: SLO definitions, contract format, test layers, alert routing, and the incident process.

s10.title: A full design round (45 minutes)
s10.prompt: Design a real-time driver earnings service: 1 million drivers check earnings 5 times a day; numbers must match payouts.
s10.deliverable: Follow the six steps: requirements, estimate, high-level design, deep dive, trade-offs, wrap-up.

s11.title: In front of the customer
s11.prompt: A logistics customer wants "AI insights on delays" in 6 weeks. Run discovery and design the smallest useful first release.
s11.deliverable: Ten discovery questions, a metric tree, a v1 scope, and a one-page proposal with risks.

s12.title: Architecture review board
s12.prompt: Present your platform to a review board. Defend three decisions and answer "what breaks at 10x?".
s12.deliverable: C4 context and container diagrams, three ADRs, and a 10x risk list.
